newsitem.title: CHINA: China says 1996 commercial tax hits 644 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China says 1996 commercial tax hits 644 bln yuan.

text.p: China collected 644.6 billion yuan ($77.6 billion) in industrial and commercial taxes in 1996, an increase of more than 100 billion yuan compared with the year before, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
Tax collectors had gathered record revenues accounting for 107 percent of the target for last year, earning them the praise of economic tsar Zhu Rongji, the official agency said.
Domestic value-added tax and consumption tax, a major part of the new revenue-sharing tax regime introduced in 1994, rose 365.7 billion yuan last year, up 14 percent, it said.
When corporate income taxes and other earnings were included, China's fiscal income hit 714.7 billion yuan in 1996, up 16.8 percent year-on-year.

"Please pass my heartfelt thanks and gratitude to all the taxation workers for the great achievements they scored in 1996," Xinhua quoted economic leader and Vice Premier Zhu as writing in a State Administration of Taxation report.
Beijing has for years struggled to boost tax revenues to try to ease widening budget deficits and finance ambitious infrastructure and social spending plans.
